summary: The ordinary prover acquired a checked five-line training proof of implication reflexivity. The second fixed donor search crossed the Python memory threshold, so the two-proof acquisition requirement was not met.
interpretation: The first proof is an elementary instance produced through generic implication introduction and hypothesis discharge. The second run returned no proof; its memory failure is not a logical refutation. This cohort is closed with STOP_ACQUISITION. Cluster extraction and holdout search did not proceed.
contribution_assessment: One fresh ordinary training derivation establishes a small acquisition capability. No receptor library, learned marking, RL policy, mapped cluster transfer or measured GCTS advantage exists in this cohort.
next_step: Design a common ordinary prover that handles negation directly and works with input subformulas, reconstructing every result into the same primitive FPC checker. Add bounded charged observations of search-state growth. Then freeze a separate, more varied non-wrapper training and holdout study. Two admitted donors and checked cluster expansions into a new complete proof remain the gate before testing learned selection.
